title: TEA Synchronized With Natural Breathing for EPS
official: Transcutaneous Electrical Acustimulation Synchronized With Natural Breathing for Epigastric Pain Syndrome
summary:
The goal of this study is to assess the acceptance and usability as well as safety of the AutoSTEA device is in treating epigastric pain syndrome in adults. It will also explore preliminary clinical and mechanistic signals. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the AutoSTEA device ease epigastric pain symptoms?
* Is the AutoSTEA device safe and feasible for patients to use at their home?

Participants will:

* Use the device for 30-60 minutes at home each day for 4 weeks
* Have a phone check-in four times through the trial (once a week).
* Answer the daily and weekly questionnaires which consist of questions regarding symptoms, device usability, and adverse events experienced.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* At least 18 years of age
* Diagnosed with epigastric pain syndrome according to Rome V Criteria
* Experienced epigastric pain at least 3 days a week for at least 3 months
* Must have normal esophagogastroduodenoscopy performed in last 2 years

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any history of gastritis, gastric/duodenal ulcers, or other organic upper GI diseases
* Current drug or alcohol abuse
* Currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant
* History of major abdominal surgery
* History of severe mental illness
* Total knee-replacement surgery or above-the-knee amputation
* Any unstable or uncontrolled medical disorders
* Current use of proton pump inhibitors, anti-nausea medications, or other functional dyspepsia treatments UNLESS regimen has remained unchanged and stable over last 3 months
* Current use of anti-depressants or NSAIDs
* Having any implanted electrical devices (pacemakers, defibrillators, neurostimulators, or any other implanted electrical devices).
* Not being fluent in English
* Having prior significant experience/knowledge with acupuncture
